blocks.heading_context: ## The Big Picture: Cooking as Technology
blocks.text:
COOKING AS COMPOUNDING TECHNOLOGY
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FIRE & COOKING        AGRICULTURE          PRESERVATION         INDUSTRIALIZATION
~1,000,000 BP         ~10,000 BP           ~5,000 BP → cont.    ~200 years ago
     │                     │                    │                     │
     ▼                     ▼                    ▼                     ▼
External digestion   Sedentary surplus    Trade networks        Caloric abundance
Brain growth         State formation      Urban civilization    Global homogenization
Social bonding       Division of labor    Long voyages          Chronic disease shift
     │                     │                    │                     │
     └─────────────────────┴────────────────────┴─────────────────────┘
                                  │
                                  ▼
                         GLOBAL FOOD SYSTEM
                 7.8B people fed by ~12 plant species
                 and 5 animal species at industrial scale

DEEP TIME ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────► PRESENT
    │
    ├── ~3.5 Mya: Oldowan tools, animal marrow access
    │
    ├── ~1 Mya: Hearth use (Wonderwerk Cave, South Africa)
    │            Wrangham: cooked food → gut shortening → larger brain
    │
    ├── ~300 kya: Consistent fire use, Neanderthal cooking
    │
    ├── ~10,500 BP: Cereal domestication, Fertile Crescent
    │
    ├── ~6,000 BP: Mesopotamian beer civilization
    │             Egyptian grain economy, pharaonic bread factories
    │
    ├── ~500 BCE: Greek symposium, Roman garum trade networks
    │
    ├── ~1000 CE: Medieval spice trade, Venice/Genoa intermediaries
    │             Salting, smoking, pickling as preservation technology
    │             Monastic brewing, distillation
    │
    ├── 1492–1600: Columbian Exchange — most transformative food event in history
    │              Potato/tomato/chile/chocolate/maize → Old World
    │              Wheat/cattle/sugar/pigs → New World
    │
    ├── 1700s–1800s: Haute cuisine codification (Carême → Escoffier)
    │               Canning (Appert 1809), mechanical refrigeration (1876)
    │               Industrialized slaughter, Birdseye freezing (1924)
    │
    ├── 1900s: Global food systems, processed food rise, Green Revolution
    │
    └── Present: Farm-to-table reaction, fermentation revival,
                lab-grown meat, food system critique

NEW WORLD → OLD WORLD                OLD WORLD → NEW WORLD
────────────────────                 ──────────────────────
Potato      → Irish staple           Wheat     → American bread
            → European caloric base  Cattle    → Great Plains beef
Tomato      → Italian "tradition"    Pigs      → forest clearing tool
Chile       → Indian/Thai/Korean     Sugar     → Caribbean plantation
Maize       → African staple         Horses    → Plains Indian warfare
Chocolate   → European obsession     Coffee    → transplanted to Americas
Vanilla     → global flavoring       Citrus    → Florida/California
Turkey      → European poultry       Honeybees → pollination dependency
